Homes built to survive what’s coming. Ready in 60 days.

We design, build and finance housing that stands up to fire, earthquake and flood, starting with backyard homes in Los Angeles.

Well housed is well.

The problem

The LA fires made it plain: we’ve built the wrong houses in the wrong places.

The problem

More than 80% of new California homes are built in high fire-risk areas.

Source: ClimateCheck

And people aren’t moving away. So the homes themselves have to change.

The problem

The way we build now is too slow, too expensive, and not fire-safe.

  • Permits

    6–12 months

  • Construction

    1–2 years

  • Landscape

    The land around homes puts them at risk

  • Fireproofing

    Design and materials aren’t fire resistant

  • Labor

    Costs per unit keep rising

  • Materials

    Costs keep rising, with high embedded carbon

Our answer

Disaster-resilient by design. Move in within 60 days.

  • Built for fire, earthquake, tornado, hurricane and flood
  • Expandable and customizable
  • No energy bills
  • Built green
  • Well designed

First product

A backyard home for Los Angeles, available now.

Our first product is an ADU (accessory dwelling unit): a self-contained home that goes on an existing lot.

How we deliver

We group buyers into 50-unit orders, then build them like a production line.

Manufacturing partner Assembly OSM provides turnkey production of prefab homes for cities.

What the homes are made of

Materials chosen to resist fire, and to lower carbon.

Superwood can replace up to 80% of steel and concrete, and protects homes from fire, insects and extreme weather.

Fire-resistant hempcrete panels, made with hemp grown on Indigenous land.

Global engineering firm with more than 50 years of fire safety engineering and 300-plus fire engineers worldwide.
